sourceNote: The fox mesh (assets/models/fox/fox.glb, assets/models/fox/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist, and arms 1.21 times longer. tools/blender/fox_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. fox.glb stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/fox_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, because the seated bind of the app depends on them.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the skin normals with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). This removes a thin dark slit and a dark wedge at the back of the armpit.
rootNormals.elbowNote: The faces within 0.07 units of each elbow joint take the skin normals too. The seated bind bends each elbow, and without this rule the split normals show a crease in the lit forearm. The tan fox shares the rig.

raise.note: The rest shape of the right arm: the mean turns of the rest samples of the fox violinist. It smooths the posed tube from the second upper arm segment to the wrist (raise_shape() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the inner elbow shows no bright streak. The fade keeps it off the play.

armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube and the socket does not fold.
armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments. Each elbow and wrist has a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the rings of its joint in the bind. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings (gap of tools/blender/fox_arms.py).

name: Fox

app.note: The scale is 1.5504 m for each unit: 1.3 times the scale that puts the standing head top at 1.083 m, the head top of the parametric fox. The leg factor raises the standing shoulder joint to 0.715 units (1.108536 m). The reach 0.5452 m holds a full violin.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 does not stretch the arms in the rig. The arms of fox-arms.glb are already 1.21 times longer than the source arms (step_shape() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py, called by tools/blender/fox_arms.py), so the reach stays app.reach.
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.09 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The chair of the app fits the legs.
headFactorNote: The factor of the head and the ears around the neck joint, for a larger head. The weights blend the growth over the neck. A larger factor turns a thin face between the neck and the head over. The export keeps the head before the factor for the holds (ungrown() of tools/studio-body.ts).
neckFactorNote: The factor of the neck length between the neck joint and the head joint. The head and the ears keep their size and move down with the head joint, 5.6 cm from the neck joint. The export moves the head center of the holds with the head (headRig() of tools/studio-body.ts).
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, +z forward, +x the left side. The tail has two bones. The elbow, forearm twist, wrist, and paw joints are the joints of the longer arms (source_joints() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py).

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as seated string players sit tall. The pelvis turns back until the hip angle opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share. The head share is 0, so that the flute hold does not fold the neck.
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of the left arm turns 110 degrees about its bind forearm toward supination (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bind paw sets the zero of the paw twist, so the left paw does not twist through 180 degrees on the violin or the flute. The right paw keeps the bind arms.
studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and 8 degrees out, so that the hips stay above the knees, and the shin is vertical (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 8 0).

weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the stretch share fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp, because a ramp folds the trunk below the right armpit.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units).

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag when a joint bends. With head, the head takes the rule too.

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. Thus the bow arm does not drag a face of the right chest. The clavicle joint is at y 0.635.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. Thus a raised bow arm does not drag the side of the neck.
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values of the rabbit, scaled by the neck of the fox.
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the long thigh turns onto the seat with no fold at the hip crease.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only. The vertices within radius of the tail line and behind the plane z = behind follow the two tail bones with soft shares.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh fox --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

flip.note: The long edge of an arm face with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units).

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of an arm or leg joint. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings).

shift.note: The orange fur moves in Oklch (shift_colors() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py) to the red-orange of orchestra-latest.png: the lightness 0.745 times, the chroma 1.21 times, and the hue 12 degrees toward red. The white fur, the black legs and ear backs, and the gloss eyes and nose keep their colors.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean color of the texture at a grid of samples. A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples are below dark. The eye box and the nose box find the eye faces and the nose faces. Then palette and shift set the color.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark eye faces to at most points points of their edge, lifted lift units. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5).

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.17). The front edge ends where the sloped thighs leave the seat top.

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Each vertex moves share of the way to the middle of its neighbors in rounds rounds. The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), because the buttocks of the mesh curve up behind the hip joints. With root, the tail root moves with the haunch. The corrective shapes give the source back.

smooth.note: The rig smooths the back of the neck and the bottom of the back of the head inside the box before the growth, so that the fur spikes there do not make a dark jagged band. The export keeps the head center before the smoothing (head_shift()), so the holds keep their places.
